source.title: A Behavioral Fingerprint for Large Language Models: Provenance Tracking via Refusal Vectors

page_placements.theme: Cross-model transfer of directions: fails raw between independent models, works after an alignment map

record.tranche_reason: The study applies refusal-vector extraction to derivative and alignment-broken models and reports fingerprint similarities, testing transfer across model variants and whether alignment-breaking variants retain the vector signal. It does not test the original refusal-behavior interventions.
record.gate_note: The study computes harmful-minus-harmless activation vectors and reports their fingerprint similarities across derivatives and attacked variants. It does not report user-facing refusal rates after ablating or adding a direction, nor general-capability results. Its identification-accuracy and unrelated-family results concern provenance performance rather than the claim versions and are not included as rows. The Table 1 and Table 6 SimHash values are omitted; the 60-row limit is used for Table 1 cosine values, both Table 2 metrics, and Table 6 cosine values.
record.test_reason: The paper uses Arditi et al.'s harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction as a provenance fingerprint. It reports only how well that fingerprint works: cosine similarity to the base family, identification accuracy, and separation from unrelated families. The fingerprint is averaged over the middle 90% of layers, which differs from the single-layer, single-position direction the claim is about. No ablation, addition or weight edit is paired with any refusal-rate or capability measure, in any model. So no version (V1 causal mediation, V2 removal, V3 jailbreak mechanism, V6 functional transfer) is tested. The cross-variant similarity values are a stability score for the authors' own method. They are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that refusal-vector fingerprints are family-specific, with near-zero similarity between unrelated models. They find them robust to quantization, LoRA, SFT and merging, with 100% Top-1 identification over 76 offspring. Pruning and distillation weaken the fingerprint strongly. Alignment-breaking attacks cut similarity to about 0.5, which stays above unrelated-family levels, so the drop also serves as a forensic signal of safety tampering.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activations and cosine similarity, but aggregates selected layer vectors into a model fingerprint for provenance tracking rather than testing refusal behavior through per-layer and per-position ablation or addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports lower similarity for merges than several other common modifications and lower similarity for pruning and distillation than for the four principal modification types. Its ablation study reports fingerprint stability with N = 500 prompts and robust identification across α ∈ [0.3, 0.7], but these are extraction-configuration results rather than refusal-behavior outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: A layer-averaged difference-in-means vector stays highly similar across derivatives. Cosine to the base family is 0.97–0.99 under quantization, about 0.80–0.96 under LoRA, 0.68–0.93 under SFT and 0.67–0.79 under merges. It is much lower for pruning (about 0.29–0.34) and distillation (about 0.53–0.63).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The geometry of the harmful-minus-harmless direction is largely preserved across common derivatives of a model family, without any functional check.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated and jailbroken Llama-3-8B variants keep a fingerprint cosine of about 0.47–0.50 to the reference. The reference model is unclear.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After abliteration or jailbreak fine-tuning, a measurable harmful-minus-harmless direction persists and is partly aligned with the original.

fits_no_version.finding: Independently trained 7B models have near-orthogonal fingerprints (|cos| < 0.03, Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal directions are family-specific and do not align across independently trained models.

record.problems: No refusal-behavior or general-capability outcomes are reported, so the study cannot establish the causal or practical-removal claims. The alignment-breaking comparison contains only two variants. Table 1 does not identify the specific derivative checkpoints associated with each family-by-modification score.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Table 1 SimHash scores and Table 6 SimHash scores. Table 1 cosine values and both Table 2 measures were retained; Table 6 cosine values were retained for the tested attack version.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction and no refusal or capability measure.
An abliterated model is included, but only its fingerprint similarity is measured, not its refusal rate.
No jailbreak-mechanism analysis and no adversarial training against ablation.
No comparison of one direction against affine, cone or multi-direction accounts.
Harmfulness and refusal are not separated.
Geometric similarity across variants is reported, but not whether the base direction still mediates refusal in the variants. No cross-lingual or base-to-instruct test.
The only reasoning model, DeepSeek-R1-Distill, appears just as a fingerprint-similarity entry.

missing.what: Cross-family fingerprint cosine matrix for 8 independently trained 7B models, all near zero. A researcher on V6 would want it, although it is not a test of the claim.
Prompt-count ablation: N=500 prompts gives cosine above 0.98 to the 10k-prompt direction. Stability across layer-window alpha 0.3–0.7.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V3/V6 labels are overturned. The V3 'supports' label in particular rested on a fingerprint drop that says nothing about how attacks work. Internal inconsistencies: the Discussion says the fingerprint is robust 'even after… pruning', but Section 5.1 calls pruning destructive. The text says standard derivatives exceed 0.80, but several Table 1 cells are below 0.8. Section 5.3 cites 76 offspring while Table 4 uses 48. The attacked variants are Llama-3-8B while the listed base is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. No code or confidence intervals are given.

versions.untested_parts: No direction ablation or addition, refusal-behavior measurement, or general-capability check.
No weight-edit intervention with a measure of refusal behavior. Abliterated variants are assessed only by fingerprint similarity.

The study reports fingerprint similarity for two alignment-breaking variants but does not establish causally that the attacks work by suppressing the direction. It does not train against ablation or test added robustness.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests derivative-model fingerprint similarity, but not transfer across languages or a controlled base-to-instruct comparison.
Fine-tuned derivatives are included, but the study does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
No reasoning-model comparison or reasoning-specific intervention.

rows.check: Fingerprint cosine 0.4746 for failspy/llama-3-8b-instruct-abliterated-v3. The repo is a Llama-3-8B (not 3.1) model, and the reference fingerprint it was compared with is not stated. The comparison may be Llama-3 against Llama-3.1, which confounds the drop. No refusal rate is reported, so the row cannot bear on V2 or V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

labels.label: none
labels.reason: No version is tested. There are no refusal-behaviour or causal measures, and the layer-averaged fingerprint is a different construct from the single direction. Its similarity across fine-tunes fits no version.

unmatched_labels.label: none
unmatched_labels.reason: No version is tested. There are no refusal-behaviour or causal measures, and the layer-averaged fingerprint is a different construct from the single direction. Its similarity across fine-tunes fits no version.

relation.reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. as its foundation and uses the direction as a tool. It never checks that the extracted vector mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: The paper builds a provenance fingerprint from Arditi-style difference-in-means vectors averaged over layers. It reports only fingerprint performance: cosine and SimHash similarity, Top-1 accuracy, margins and FSR. It has no ablation, no addition and no refusal rate in any model. The cross-variant cosines in Tables 1 and 2 are the method's robustness metric, not a test of V6 transfer.

source_check.notes: The paper's prose overstates its tables. It says standard derivatives exceed 0.80 or 0.9, but Table 1 gives SFT 0.681-0.934 and merges 0.669-0.785. The Discussion calls the fingerprint robust to pruning, but Table 2 gives 0.29-0.34. The Table 6 attacked models are Llama-3-8B (abliterated-v3: 0.4746) with no stated reference fingerprint, so the similarity drop may mix the 3 to 3.1 version change with the attack.

statements.correction: Table 5 covers 8 independently trained models at 7B scale (Mistral, Granite, InternLM2, Baichuan2, Qwen2.5, Llama2, BLOOM, Llama3.1). Off-diagonal cosines run from -0.018 to 0.031, so max |cos| = 0.031. The mean |cos| computed from the table is about 0.012; the text claims an average below 0.01 and pairs 'consistently below 0.1'. The fingerprint is the mean of unit-normalized per-layer difference-in-means vectors (final token, middle 90% of layers).
statements.problem: The bound |cos| < 0.03 is wrong. Table 5 has off-diagonal cosines of 0.030 and 0.031. 'No rows extracted' conflicts with the pack's count of 60 rows in the record.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Quantization, adapters, and fine-tunes with Table 1 cosine similarity at least 0.8
reader_labels.reason: Derivative fingerprints remain similar to their base-family reference in these settings (R01-R03, R05-R07, R09-R11, R13-R14, R17, R19, R21-R23, R25-R26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Lower Table 1 scores and pairwise comparisons involving pruning or distillation
reader_labels.reason: Similarity is lower for some merges, fine-tunes, and adapter cases, and the authors specifically report pruning and distillation as destructive to the fingerprint (R04, R08, R12, R15-R16, R18, R20, R24, R27-R28, R31-R38, R43-R58).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Both variants have reduced similarity to the corresponding fingerprint, consistent with a weakened direction signal; the measurements do not establish that suppression causes the attacks to work (R59-R60).
